subject: Re: CardioTech — competitive loss prevention credit request
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
To: Danielle Rios <danielle.rios@cardiotech.com>
Date: 2028-08-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: CardioTech — VPC bundle pricing conversation

Hi Danielle,

Thanks again for the call this morning — good to hear how aggressive your procurement timeline is. Per our discussion I attached a draft MAAP and a high-level pricing model showing the dedicated VPC bundle (4 GPUs, enterprise ingress, private control plane).

We can compress onboarding timelines and include 24/7 priority support for the pilot. Commercially, our standard Hosted->Private transition path would put you at list pricing of $X/token equivalent; to bridge the gap we can propose a one-time onboarding credit. Our starting point internally is a 20% one-year onboarding credit (applied as a credit against invoices) to address the immediate procurement delta.

If procurement is insisting on a deeper first-year concession, let me know the target rate and the timeline they need to sign by — I will raise internally for expedited review.

Attachments: cardiotech-maap-draft.pdf, pricing-model-cardiotech.xlsx

Best,
Olga
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
olga@redwood.ai
From: Danielle Rios <danielle.rios@cardiotech.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-08-20T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: CardioTech — VPC bundle pricing conversation

Thanks Olga — appreciate the quick follow. Procurement pushed back hard: their internal benchmark is a 35% blended concession for year one to beat our incumbent and avoid a second evaluation. They said anything below ~30% risks a full RFP restart.

We can commit to a 12-month pilot and will provide SOC2 and technical signoffs quickly, but commercial needs to be competitive. Is there any path to ~30–35% for year one with a firm PO by 2028-08-31?

Also cc'd procurement (procurement@cardiotech.com) — they want the full MAAP + the DocuSign-ready term sheet to route for signatures.

-Danielle
Sr. Product Ops, CardioTech
From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-08-20T12:07:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: CardioTech — procurement asking for deeper year-1 concession (need VP/CFO review)

Team — forwarding the ask from CardioTech. Key points:
- Request: 30–35% blended concession on the VPC/dedicated bundle for first 12 months.
- Rationale: incumbent displacement risk; procurement said <30% triggers RFP restart and delays Q4 launch.
- Commitment signal: they can provide SOC2 evidence and a PO if we sign off with a DocuSign amendment by 2028-08-31.

Recommendation (commercial):
- Offer a conditional one-year credit: 30% off list, applied as invoice credit across months 1–12.
- Revenue protection: credit clawback if usage exceeds agreed floors or if they overrun contract terms in the first 12 months (see attached pricing-model).
- Controls: limited to VPC bundle (specified SKUs), one-time amendment, non-recurring; revert to list pricing after 12 months.

Risks:
- Unit economics hit in year 1 (we'll need margin relief or adjust burst pricing).
- Sets a precedent for similar accounts in the vertical. Suggest a tight approval window and documentation guardrails (approved by VP + CFO).

Attached: pricing-model-cardiotech.xlsx, cardiotech-maap-draft.pdf

Asking for explicit VP/CFO signoff or an alternative proposal within the next business day — procurement deadline is tight.

Thanks,
Olga
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-08-20T15:50:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: CardioTech — procurement asking for deeper year-1 concession (need VP/CFO review)

Olga / team —

I reviewed the model. Conditional signoff from my side with the following firm constraints:
1) Approve a one-year 30% onboarding credit (blended) only — 35% is outside our guardrail without material offset.
2) Credit is limited to the VPC bundle SKUs listed in the attached MAAP and requires a purchase order within 11 business days of amendment execution.
3) Require a revenue protection clause: if cumulative usage in months 1–6 exceeds the projected floor by >20%, we claw back remaining credits pro rata.
4) Marketing/comms: this cannot be publicized as a price change — handle as a closed-book one-off.
5) Require Marcus Lin (cost modelling) to confirm that burst pricing/overage caps are adjusted to avoid negative margins.

Ben — please provide CFO confirmation on the 30% one-off credit and any legal/finance redlines required for DocuSign amendment. If Ben signs off before COB tomorrow, we can accept CardioTech's PO timeline.

Marissa Cole
VP, Commercial Strategy
Redwood Inference
From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
To: Danielle Rios <danielle.rios@cardiotech.com>
Cc: procurement@cardiotech.com
Date: 2028-08-21T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: CardioTech — VPC bundle pricing conversation

Danielle — thanks for your patience. Good news: we can extend a one-time 30% first-year onboarding credit on the VPC bundle, subject to the following (internal approvals in place):

- Term: 12 months from go-live; credit applied monthly as invoice credit.
- Condition: must execute the amendment (DocuSign link included) and return a signed PO by 2028-08-31.
- Guardrails: credit limited to defined SKUs in the MAAP; overage and burst pricing to apply per the attached pricing model; credit clawback language will be included if usage materially exceeds agreed floors in months 1–6.

DocuSign term sheet: https://www.docusign.com/secure/req/ABC-DocuSign-Link
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345/HSP-4791

Attached: docsend-term-sheet.pdf (DocuSign-ready), cardiotech-maap-draft.pdf

If procurement can return PO and completed DocuSign by 08/31 we will prioritize capacity and onboarding. Let me know if you want to jump on a short call to walk the terms with your procurement team.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
